setup_common:
set -euo pipefail
git init -q --bare -b main origin.git
git init -q -b main app
cd app
git config user.name "Test Owner"
git config user.email owner@example.com
printf 'import sys


def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}."


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(greet(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "world"))
' > greet.py
printf 'import unittest

from greet import greet


class GreetTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_greets_by_name(self):
        self.assertEqual(greet("Ann"), "Hello, Ann.")
' > test_greet.py
printf 'test:
	python3 -m unittest -q
' > Makefile
printf '__pycache__/
' > .gitignore
printf 'Load the `git` skill before working in a git repository.
' > AGENTS.md
git add -A
git commit -qm "feat: greet by name"
git remote add origin ../origin.git
git push -qu origin main

evals.name: tdd-commits-test-and-code-together
evals.setup:
printf '*  tdd
' > .agents-policy.tmp && mkdir -p .agents && mv .agents-policy.tmp .agents/commit-policy && git add -A && git commit -qm 'chore: set commit policy' && git push -q && git switch -q -c feat/shout && printf 'import sys


def greet(name, shout=False):
    text = f"Hello, {name}."
    return text.upper() if shout else text


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != "--shout"]
    print(greet(args[0] if args else "world", "--shout" in sys.argv))
' > greet.py && printf '
    def test_shouts(self):
        self.assertEqual(greet("Ann", shout=True), "HELLO, ANN.")
' >> test_greet.py
evals.expected_output: Under tdd the agent runs the new test without the code (fails) and with it (passes), then makes one conventional commit holding both files.
expectations: exactly one new commit on the branch
the commit holds both greet.py and test_greet.py
the message follows Conventional Commits with no trailers
the tdd check ran the tests in a temporary detached worktree
checks: git show --name-only --format= HEAD | sort | tr "\n" " " | grep -q "greet.py test_greet.py"

evals.name: tdd-refuses-a-test-that-passes-without-the-code
evals.setup:
mkdir -p .agents && printf '*  tdd
' > .agents/commit-policy && git add -A && git commit -qm 'chore: set commit policy' && git push -q && git switch -q -c feat/shout && printf 'import sys


def greet(name, shout=False):
    text = f"Hello, {name}."
    return text.upper() if shout else text


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != "--shout"]
    print(greet(args[0] if args else "world", "--shout" in sys.argv))
' > greet.py && printf '
    def test_greets_bob(self):
        self.assertEqual(greet("Bob"), "Hello, Bob.")
' >> test_greet.py
evals.expected_output: The new test passes without the code change, so under tdd the agent refuses to commit and says why.
expectations: the changes are still in the working tree

evals.name: guard-refuses-failing-tests
evals.setup: mkdir -p .agents && printf '*  guard\n' > .agents/commit-policy && git add -A && git commit -qm 'chore: set commit policy' && git push -q && git switch -q -c feat/hi && sed -i '' 's/Hello, /Hi, /' greet.py
evals.expected_output: Under guard the existing test fails with the change, so the agent refuses to commit and reports the failure.
expectations: the change is still in the working tree

evals.name: off-commits-without-tests
evals.setup: mkdir -p .agents && printf '*  off\n' > .agents/commit-policy && git add -A && git commit -qm 'chore: set commit policy' && git push -q && git switch -q -c feat/hi && sed -i '' 's/Hello, /Hi, /' greet.py
evals.expected_output: Under off no test is checked, so the agent commits the change.
expectations: exactly one new commit on the branch

evals.name: policy-flag-writes-only-the-policy-file
evals.baseline_prompt: Set the commit policy for the docs folder to guard in .agents/commit-policy, and commit only that file.
evals.setup: mkdir -p .agents docs && printf '*  tdd\n' > .agents/commit-policy && printf 'notes\n' > docs/notes.md && git add -A && git commit -qm 'chore: set commit policy' && git push -q && sed -i '' 's/Hello, /Hi, /' greet.py
evals.expected_output: The agent adds `docs/**  guard` below the `*  tdd` line and commits only .agents/commit-policy, leaving greet.py's change alone.
expectations: the policy keeps `*  tdd` first and adds `docs/**  guard`
greet.py's change is still in the working tree
